sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Water hemlock is a perennial of marshes, ditches and waterside margins across northern Eurasia. It grows about 50–120 cm tall and bears a hollow stem, finely divided leaves and white umbels. The rhizome and roots have partitioned cavities.

sections.title: Severe toxicity
sections.text: All parts are extremely poisonous, especially the rhizome, which contains cicutoxin and related compounds; ingestion can cause seizures and severe poisoning. Do not gather or eat it. The plate accurately shows wet habitat, leaves, umbels and a cross-section of the chambered rhizome.
